Mutations in TGFBI disrupt the integrin-mediated signaling pathway, contributing to epithelial basement membrane dystrophy. Concurrently, mutations in HSPG2 disrupt basement membrane assembly and organization, leading to Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1. Both pathways converge on the integrity of the basement membrane, with disruptions in its assembly and organization manifesting as the respective phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in TGFBI or HSPG2 do not lead to loss-of-function or that the downstream pathways they affect are completely independent and do not converge on any common cellular process related to basement membrane structure. _(variant: Identification of common, benign variants in gnomAD within the coding regions of TGFBI or HSPG2 that are associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared dependence on basement membrane integrity, despite distinct genetic origins, may reveal therapeutic targets that could address common downstream molecular defects in both epithelial basement membrane dystrophy and Schwartz-Jampel syndrome type 1, potentially improving treatments for ocular and skeletal manifestations.
